_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel finally backed off the record — $6.382 for the week of 9/28, down 14.7 cents, with Gulf crude flowing again. Reprice your fuel surcharge off the current index so you stay fair with shippers, but don't let it drag your linehaul down with it: spot rates are still climbing, so hold your base rate. Reefer's linehaul is easing as produce winds down — don't chase it, but Yakima-to-East-Coast apples are still paying $12.6k+ a load, so push those.

_sourcing.status: FIFTEENTH straight cycle with WebFetch/curl egress blocked (eia.gov WebFetch = EGRESS_BLOCKED; curl to eia.gov/dat.com = CONNECT tunnel 403). WebSearch only. asOf advanced 2026-09-21 -> 2026-09-28: EIA diesel (week 9/28, multi-source), DAT all-in (week 9/20-26, Overdrive/TheTrucker), USDA AMS (week ended 9/29) all reflect this window. The EIA week-of-10/5 print was NOT found in any source as of 10/6, so asOf is NOT advanced past 9/28.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE, CONFLICT RESOLVED. $6.382/gal for EIA week ending 2026-09-28, down $0.147 from the $6.529 record of 9/21 (arithmetic checks) — first decline after three straight record weeks. Confirmed by 5+ independent outlets: FreightWaves benchmark-diesel piece (9/29, 'More oil out of the Gulf translating to lower prices'), Logistics Management ('National diesel average heads down for first time in 12 weeks'), Overdrive (9/30), FleetOwner ('Diesel drops 15c nationally to $6.38'), IndexBox, weeklydiesel.com/thetrading.tools. The earlier FreightWaves 'up 10 cents to just under $6.57' item (Margin Squeeze) is a different/non-EIA series and does not describe the EIA 9/28 print; disregarded. Context: CME ULSD hit record settle $5.262 on 9/16, fell to $4.6847 by 9/25 (rebound after); crude flows out of the Persian Gulf nearing pre-war levels. NOT USED: AAA retail $6.32 on 10/5 (non-EIA retail survey, rejected as a figure) — directionally suggests the 10/5 EIA print is lower again but is unconfirmed. Next cycle: pull EIA week of 10/5.
_sourcing.trend: Flipped up -> down on the confirmed EIA decline (diesel-driven). Caveat: all-in spot (NTI) and DAT linehaul for van are still firm/rising, so 'down' reflects fuel easing, not freight rates falling.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: PROMOTED (flagged). $3.53/mi, FreightWaves SONAR NTI (dry van incl. fuel) 'climbed back to $3.53' per FreightWaves 'Truckload's mixed signals' (published ~10/4; reading ~10/2-3). Up from $3.42 (9/16). Cross-checks: FreightWaves 9/28 piece implied ~$3.45 (5.2% above $3.28); one other summary showed $3.55. Single clean source and the exact reading date is approximate (~10/3), so medium confidence; this is newer than asOf 9/28 by a few days.
_sourcing.modality: DAT all-in, week 9/20-26 (Overdrive 9/30 quoting DAT; TheTrucker 'Load posts down 1%'): Dry Van $3.01 (reported +5c; linehaul $2.17 held flat — fuel was the entire move), Reefer PROMOTED $3.59 -> $3.63 (+4c; linehaul $2.71 FELL — fuel more than accounted for the rise), Flatbed PROMOTED to $3.60 (+5c; linehaul $2.59 fell). FLAG: van $3.01 / +5c also matches the earlier AJOT 9/13-19 headline, so one of the two weeks may be mislabeled by sources; van held at $3.01 rather than guess. REEFER SOFTENING: first visible — reefer linehaul fell, and Truckstop/FTR broker-posted reefer rates 'slid as expected' (Overdrive 9/30). All-in still up only because of the fuel pass-through; with diesel now falling, expect reefer all-in to roll over next cycle. yoy fields unchanged (DAT linehaul yoy, older reading; search summaries were inconsistent on newer values, so not touched). LTL and Intermodal unchanged, no new data.
_sourcing.commodityRates: General Dry Freight 3.01 (tracks dry van all-in). Frozen Seafood/Poultry and Fresh Produce PROMOTED 3.59 -> 3.63 (tracks reefer all-in). Coiled Steel 3.57 and High-Value Electronics 2.60 carried forward unchanged (Coiled Steel not re-mapped to the new $3.60 flatbed all-in; needs a decision/refresh).
_sourcing.lanes: Yakima, WA -> Northeast (reefer) REFRESHED LIVE: USDA AMS refrigerated truck rates, week ended 2026-09-29, via IndexBox summary of agtransport.usda.gov: Boston midpoint $12,650, New York $12,600 (Miami $14,150 for reference). Down from prior week (Boston $13,650 -> $12,650; NY $12,950 -> $12,600) — first sign of Yakima easing. Range shown covers only the two Northeast lanes confirmed for 9/29; Baltimore/Philadelphia 9/29 midpoints not confirmed (Philadelphia $11,500 and Baltimore $11,700 are from 9/22). Atlanta -> Miami: CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged, 16 cycles — only generic broker/blog ranges ($2.20-3.00 reefer) surfaced, no clean dated absolute $/mi; NOT promoted. Memphis -> Atlanta: not searched, unchanged.
_sourcing.blurb: Rewritten around the confirmed diesel decline (reprice surcharge off the index, do not let it drag linehaul), firm spot rates, reefer linehaul easing, and Yakima still strong at $12.6k+.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: (1) EIA week of 10/5 not yet found — likely another decline per AAA $6.32 but unconfirmed. (2) Van $3.01 duplicated across two DAT weeks in sources; confirm 9/20-26 vs 9/13-19. (3) spotAllIn $3.53 is a single-source ~10/3 reading. (4) Atlanta->Miami needs a clean dated absolute $/mi (try AMS Southeast district report). (5) Watch reefer all-in roll over as diesel falls and produce season ends; Yakima Boston/NY already down ~$1,000 and ~$350 w/w.
